Tile (49, 54): cell 49 * 50 + 54 = 2504, past the 2,500-byte grids. g_tileType[2504] = 0x00572cb0 = byte 0 of g_habitatSlots, 0 in the segment image cov_k3_camera/03 = type 0 `tees`, flags word (+0x2c) 4, so the height step is sy -= (g_tileLevel[cell] - 3) * S * Z / 4 with S = f_w_4c2e00[0] = 5, Z = g_zoomScale = 4. g_tileLevel[2504] = 0x005439e0 = byte 0 of g_surfaces5439e0[0], which holds the vtable 0x004ba2d8 that Surface_ctor stores (0x00473ab7; initGlobalArray_00404c20's step 0x00404c85 constructs the 16 elements): 0xd8 = -40, (-43) * 5 * 4 / 4 = -215, sy + 215. The neighbour corner (0xc400, 0xd7ff) is cell 2503 = 0x005439df = 0: sy + 15. Base 300 and 281; with the byte 0 the corner would be (431, 296), level with the opposite corner (368, 295). The port's GameState holds 0 at 0x005439e0 (its boot runs no Surface_ctor), so the port draws a regular diamond. Not fixed: storing the vtable word needs an exe .rdata address in the port's GameState (decision, 26_notes.md).

[roadmap S3.26] P4's selected-golfer sprite with f_w_4c2e00[2] = -2 reads `golfer -2` (0x005792b8), inside g_sprites5791f8: +8 / +0xc = element 4's +0x18 / +0x1c (cut 80 x 80 in all 205 segment start images) and the byte +0x21 = byte 1 of element 5's handle +4 (a jgld Sprite heap pointer). The port answers the handle byte as 1 whenever the backend holds element 5's sprite (gfx_sprite_ref_read): the byte is nonzero in all 205 recorded images, but its value is a heap address byte the port does not reproduce, so a heap pointer whose byte 1 is 0 (the original then draws nothing) is not modelled. Other negative selection words (f_w_4c2e00[2] = -4 in 16 images) read other objects: only reads that land in a SpriteRef the backend holds, at +0x10..+0x24 or the handle, are answered; any other read takes the GameState word (0 for pointer-class objects).

text: [roadmap S3.26] gfx.poll_position: a checkpoint whose POLL record has the pos of a FRAME record rode on that frame's head clock call (trace_schema.md: a record at pos n is written inside or after clock call n - 1), so its snapshot position is pos - 1 and the frame's own cursor reads (also at pos n) take it. Measured on cov_k3_camera2 y_inj4: S3.25's call log has 153 resetSpriteQueue calls at the poll (frame 153 had not drawn) and the sprays' column = g_date 152 mod 13; with S3.16's rule the snapshot fell at frame 154's first cursor read, after frame 153's present (the port's state there held g_date 155 against the checkpoint's 153). 9 of 688 pinned checkpoints have such a POLL (cov_a_flags ztut / zdemo, cov_a_keys3 season, cov_b_holes18 holes, cov_k1_paths cart, cov_k1_river r20, cov_k1_routing end, cov_k3_camera2 y_inj4, cov_l_bridge obj5). The rule was not checked on a recording that puts a present between a frame head and the frame's first cursor read (none of the 9 has one).
